## Context / Problem

`958e-f4b3-275c-4154` made the write-path drain gate O(1) on a **quiet** store by caching
"nothing can be pending before T" in `.rebar/enrich-gate.json`. The marker is only ever
*written* on a scan that found nothing:

```python
# src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py:374-377
if out:
    _clear_gate_marker(tracker)
else:
    _write_gate_marker(tracker, now_ns, soonest)
```

So a **single** pending entry is enough to disable the fast path for the entire store, and every
subsequent write pays a full walk of every ticket directory until the pending set empties again.

## Measured (2026-08-21, synthetic stores, marker forced cold)

| store size | pending | gate ms |
|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 1 | 116.9 |
| 1000 | 500 | 157.1 |
| 1000 | 1000 | 206.5 |
| 4000 | 1 | 560.3 |
| 4000 | 500 | 572.3 |
| 4000 | 0 | cold 525.7, **warm 0.110** |

- Cost is **linear in store size** (x4 tickets -> x3.6-4.8) and only weakly sensitive to backlog
  depth (x500 depth -> x1.34; x1000 -> x1.77).
- **Depth 1 already costs the full scan.** The trigger is binary, not proportional.
- The marker, when it engages, is ~4,800x faster (0.110 ms vs 525.7 ms).

On the live 4,938-ticket store this is 1,200-1,330 ms per write.

## Why this is filed separately

Found while debugging `f400-987f-45f6-419a` ("deep enrichment backlog starves late entries").
That bug's mechanism is the **selection order** (an id-sorted prefix); this one is the **marker's
all-or-nothing design**. They share a precondition (a non-empty pending set) but are distinct
mechanisms, proven by the table above: fixing fairness lets *that* store's backlog drain to
empty, which restores the marker there, but it does not help any store that keeps one entry
pending. Folding a marker redesign into a bug fix would exceed that bug's authorised scope, so
it is recorded here instead.

## Scope note (read before implementing)

`958e`'s own block comment (`queue.py:232-254`) enumerates three accepted failure modes and all
three are the marker wrongly saying *quiet*. The branch that never writes the marker at all is
implemented but discussed nowhere — not in the comment, not in the commit message, and not in
any of the 9 marker tests, every one of which seeds a store whose pending set becomes empty.

Note also that story `c1de-d6a0-6cef-4135`'s AC scopes the budget to the quiet case: *"`maybe_drain`
no-ops with no spawn **when nothing soaked**, within `DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS` (20 ms)"*. A gate that
finds a real backlog is not on that no-op path, so this is a **cost/design** improvement, not a
violated contract — size it accordingly.

`f400`'s open question #3 sketches the candidate direction: record "nothing pending BEFORE
index N" rather than all-or-nothing. That is a **design change**, so it wants a plan and a
review, not a drive-by patch.

## Approach

Generalize the gate marker from "the whole store is quiet" to "everything OUTSIDE this
recorded live set is quiet" — the set-valued form of f400's open question #3 ("nothing
pending before index N", but keyed on the queue's real membership rather than a sort
boundary). Concretely:

- `_write_gate_marker` records a third field, `live`: the ticket ids that had a live queue
  entry (enqueued, no later DONE) when the full scan ran. The full scan now ALWAYS writes
  the marker — the `if out: _clear_gate_marker(...)` branch (queue.py:374-377) goes away.
  With a non-empty pending set, `next_eligible_ns` is <= now by construction (a pending
  entry's eligible instant is its soak deadline, already past), so the marker never claims
  quiet for a noisy store.
- `_read_gate_marker` validates `live` (a list of strings, or absent/None from an older
  marker) and reports the whole marker untrusted on any wrong type, exactly like the
  existing fields — untrusted degrades to the full scan, the pre-existing behaviour.
- `pending_enrichment` gains a middle path: a TTL-fresh, non-future marker that does not
  prove quiet but carries a `live` list scopes the walk to reducing ONLY those tickets
  (`reduce_ticket` per live id — real per-entry reductions, so time-driven transitions:
  soak deadlines passing and leases expiring are still answered honestly). The full
  `os.listdir` walk remains the fallback for no/untrusted/expired markers. The per-entry
  scan loop is extracted into a helper along the existing seam so no function crosses the
  McCabe ceiling.
- Scoped probes do NOT rewrite the marker. Within a marker's lifetime the live set cannot
  grow (every queue append still clears the marker — rule 2 unchanged), and NOT refreshing
  `written_ns` preserves rule 3: the TTL still bounds the time since the last FULL walk, so
  the accepted append-during-scan race keeps exactly today's bound.

Honesty analysis (rule 1): the marker still only ever asserts ABSENCE of pending work — a
quiet store, or quiet-outside-the-live-set. Pending verdicts always come from reducing real
queue events; a stale or wrong marker can defer a drain (TTL-bounded, as today) but can
never manufacture a pending ticket. The three-rule block comment (queue.py:232-254) is
updated to document the live-set form and the previously undocumented never-writes branch's
replacement.

Cost: a probe on a store with a standing backlog drops from O(store) (full walk, ~1.2 s at
4,938 tickets) to O(live set) reductions; the quiet fast path stays O(1). This preserves
c1de's quiet-case 20 ms budget scope; the noisy-case cost now scales with the backlog, not
the store.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py` — marker read/write/validation, `pending_enrichment`
  scoped-scan path + extracted scan helper, block-comment update.
- `tests/unit/test_enrich_queue.py` — new tests below; the 9 existing marker tests must
  pass unchanged (they pin the quiet path, TTL, invalidation, and corruption handling).

No other module changes: `enrich_drain.maybe_drain` and `drain` consume
`pending_enrichment` unchanged; the marker file name, location (`.rebar` sidecar via
`StorePaths`), TTL constant, and clear-on-append call sites are untouched.

## Testing

RED first (fails on current code), all counted by instrumenting `reduce_ticket`
(`_count_reductions`), never wall clock (`check_wall_clock_asserts`):

- A store with a PERMANENTLY non-empty pending set (one eligible entry that is never
  claimed or done), parametrized over store sizes 4 and 40: after one cold scan, a repeat
  probe reduces exactly the live entries (1), independent of store size, and still returns
  the pending id. (RED: current code clears the marker and reduces all N every probe.)
- New-enqueue visibility through the scoped path: with a backlog marker standing, enqueue a
  second ticket with soak 0 — the append clears the marker, and the next probe returns both
  ids (never hides the newcomer behind the live set).
- TTL still bounds the scoped path: scoped probes do not refresh `written_ns` — a probe
  past the TTL performs a full walk again (reduction count == store size, and the marker is
  re-established by that walk).
- `live`-field validation: a marker whose `live` is wrong-typed (a string; a list with a
  non-string) is untrusted and degrades to the full scan, still returning the pending id.
- Time-driven transitions through the scoped path: a soaking live entry becomes pending
  once its deadline passes, and a claimed live entry becomes reclaimable at lease expiry,
  both answered from scoped reductions without a full walk.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A store with a standing non-empty pending set does not pay a full store walk on every write.
- [ ] The existing marker honesty rules are preserved: the cache can still only ever say
      "nothing is pending" (for the whole store or for everything outside its recorded live
      set — never manufacture a pending ticket), every queue append still invalidates it, and
      it is still TTL-bounded with the TTL measured from the last full walk.
- [ ] A test seeds a store with a **permanently non-empty** pending set and pins the gate cost
      (by probe/syscall count, not wall clock — `check_wall_clock_asserts`).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the unit sweep are green.
